newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH OPPOSITION SOC DEMS TO SEEK BUDGET CHANGES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH OPPOSITION SOC DEMS TO SEEK BUDGET CHANGES.

text.p: The parliamentary leader of the Czech Social Democrats Stanislav Gross said on Tuesday that his opposition party would seek changes to the draft state budget for 1997.
Gross told reporters that the Social Democrat (CSSD) club (parliamentary party) agreed with the centre-right government's overall policy of a balanced budget.
But he added: "The CSSD club agreed that it will ask the chamber for a statement suggesting that the government should put changes into the draft of the state budget."
The lower chamber of parliament is due to hold the first reading of the budget later on Tuesday.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's three-party coalition holds only 99 seats in the 200-seat chamber. The Social Democrats can therefore block the budget if they win full support from the two other opposition parties, the little-reformed Communists and the far-right Republicans.
Gross said the Social Democrats would seek changes to two paragraphs in the draft budget.
The first allows the government to change the budget after parliament has approved it as long as this does not affect the overall level of revenue and expenditure.
The Klaus government has been seriously weakened since it lost its parliamentary majority in elections at the end of May.
On Monday it issued a statement effectively rejecting opposition attempts to undermine its authority.
Analysts have said the budget will mark the first major policy showdown between the government and opposition, and could trigger early elections possibly next spring.

Under a deal brokered by President Vaclav Havel, the Social Democrats won key positions in parliament including the chairmanship for their leader Milos Zeman in return for supporting the Klaus coalition.
